subject: Bounded inspection parameters & pen-test scoping for Order Form
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clarionhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify inspection bands and pen-test scope for upcoming order form

Hi team,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. As we finalize the Order Form and MSA for Clarion Health, our security and procurement teams have a few clarification asks around the Security Exhibit / Audit Rights language so we can sign off internally. I've bundled the three primary items below:

1) Inspection windows and sampling bands — we need firm language describing what "bounded inspection" means operationally (e.g., limited inspection vs privileged inspection), typical sampling rates/examples, and how long artifacts will be available after an inspection window.

2) Pen test coordination — Clarion typically requires a 5 business day notice for staging access and prefers a 72-hour testing window. Please confirm Redwood's expected notification window, attack surface carveouts (if any), and whether simulated phishing or social engineering is covered under the same clause.

3) Evidence handback & delivery — we need a short runbook for evidence delivery (S3/secure share link), expected turnaround on ad-hoc requests, and how long you retain evidentiary artifacts after handback.

Attached: our current Order Form redline (OrderForm_Clarion_v1.docx) and a short SOC 2 request form so legal can map assertions to your artifact list.

Can we get a short proposal from Redwood (legal + ops) by end of day Friday so procurement can prepare the internal MRA? If it's easier, a 30-minute sync early next week would work.

Appreciate it —
Marta
Marta Ruiz
Senior Security Manager, Clarion Health
marta.ruiz@clarionhealth.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clarionhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 12:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify inspection bands and pen-test scope for upcoming order form

Marta —

Thanks for the clear list. We've discussed internally (Legal + Security + Sales Ops) and put together a concise proposal below that we think will address Clarion's compliance needs while keeping the Order Form operationally practical. If that looks reasonable we'll draft redline snippets for the MSA and Order Form and send them over.

Proposed approach (high level):

- Inspection bands: define two bands in the Security Exhibit — "Limited Inspection" (paper evidence + scoped sampling, no privileged access) and "Privileged Inspection" (temporary account/staging access with approved scope). We propose limited inspection be the default and privileged inspection granted only with 10 business days' notice and an approved Ops runbook.

- Sampling examples: for Limited Inspection, sampling defined as "up to 3 representative artifacts per assertion" or "up to 2 weekly snapshots per environment" (we'll formalize exact language). Privileged Inspection sampling will be scoped by system component and limited to the components listed in the Order Form appendix.

- Pen test notice: Redwood's standard is 72 hours for low-risk scheduled tests and 5 business days for tests requiring staging privileges. We can accept a Clarion-preferred 5 business day notice for staging access if we add an operations blackout window carveout and require a signed runbook that lists the allowable tools and a designated point of contact. Social engineering/phishing simulations will be treated separately and require explicit approval.

- Evidence delivery & retention: evidence will be delivered via a secure share link (pre-authorized S3 bucket or secure SharePoint link). We propose a 45-day retention for inspection artifacts after completion, and a 90-day retention for privileged-access logs unless otherwise required for an incident. We will provide a matrix matching SOC 2 assertions to artifact types in the redline.

Next steps:
1) Legal draft: Laura to produce MSA + Order Form redline snippets that reflect the above.
2) Ops deliverable: Olga to assemble the evidence-handback matrix and proposed retention/transfer mechanics (secure link, ACLs, temporary credentials).
3) Schedule: I'm available for a 30-min call Tue/Thu next week — propose Tue 11 AM PT.

I'll attach the internal draft (OrderForm_proposal_v1) when Laura and Olga sign off.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Customer Trust, Redwood Inference
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clarionhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Clarion Health Procurement <procurement@clarionhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify inspection bands and pen-test scope for upcoming order form

Vivek / team —

Appreciate the clear proposal. A few clarifying asks from procurement/security:

- The 10 business day timeline for privileged inspection is longer than our typical window (we usually expect 5 business days). Is the 10-day request driven by staff availability or by staging prep? Would Redwood accept 5 business days if Clarion limits requested scopes to a maximum of 2 environments per calendar quarter?

- On retention: Clarion's legal prefers a 12 month retention for transactional logs tied to SOC 2 evidence. Would Redwood consider a split approach: 90 days for full artifacts, 12 months for access/transaction logs?

- For pen tests, we need explicit confirmation that Redwood will provide a PoC point of contact and a standard list of disallowed tools (e.g., active destructive fuzzers). Please include that in the runbook.

Attached: completed SOC2_request_form.pdf with the assertions we will map. Procurement has also asked for the DocuSign flow — happy to receive a redline in Docx and we can push via DocuSign once legal is comfortable.

If you can confirm the 5-day alternative and the split retention approach, procurement is fine to proceed to MRA review.

Thanks,
Marta
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clarionhealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify inspection bands and pen-test scope for upcoming order form

Marta —

Thanks for the follow-ups and for the SOC2 form. Below are concrete legal positions and the next steps we'll take to produce redline files for your counters: 

1) Privileged inspection notice: we can accept a 5 business day notice as an alternate to the 10 business day default provided that Clarion commits in the Order Form appendix to limit requests to no more than 2 environments per quarter and provides a prioritized scope list at time of notice. We'll add language to that effect in the Order Form appendix.

2) Retention split: Redwood legal can agree to the split approach — 90 days for full artifacts, 12 months for "transactional logs" tying to SOC2 assertions. We'll include a definition of "transactional logs" and an explicit exception for incident response where longer retention may apply.

3) Pen test runbook: attached are two stubs: msa_redline_snippet.docx (proposed MSA clause for inspection rights and frequency limits) and evidence-handback-matrix.csv (operations mapping of SOC2 assertions to artifacts and retention). Key legal limits: inspections limited to once per 12 months per account unless a material incident or regulator demand arises; privileged inspections require an approved runbook, scoped list, and mutually agreed schedule; simulated social engineering expressly excluded unless separately contracted.

4) Disallowed tools: Ops will provide a non-exhaustive list of disallowed destructive tools in the runbook; this will be an operational appendix, not a legal gating list. Olga will follow up with that content.

Next steps:
- Laura to upload redlines to DocuSign-friendly .docx and share link (target: EOD Wed).
- Olga to finalize the evidence-handback matrix and the list of disallowed testing tools (target: EOD Thu).
- Vivek to confirm the 30-min alignment call if Clarion prefers synchronous review.

Attaching the two stubs now for your review. If these look good we'll generate a single redline package for procurement.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
